Steps: 1) Hold dumbbells on the floor in a high plank with feet wider than hip-width. 2) Row one dumbbell to your ribs while resisting rotation. 3) Lower it under control and alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use flat-sided dumbbells if possible and keep hips square to the floor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, upper back using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hinge forward with light dumbbells hanging under your shoulders. 2) Raise both arms out to the sides with elbows slightly bent. 3) Lower the weights slowly back under your shoulders. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use light weights and think wide elbows, not hands flying backward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, upper back using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hinge forward and hold dumbbells with palms facing behind or inward. 2) Row with elbows flaring out to the sides toward shoulder height. 3) Lower the weights until arms are long again. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the load light and avoid shrugging as elbows rise. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Pullover
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, chest, serratus using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back and hold one dumbbell over your chest with both hands. 2) Lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping ribs down. 3) Pull it back over your chest with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a controlled range and stop before your shoulders or back compensate. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell High Pull
Short Description: An at-home power strength exercise for upper back, shoulders, hips using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs and feet hip-width apart. 2) Dip slightly, then drive up and pull elbows high as the dumbbells travel upward. 3) Lower back to the start with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the weights close and lead with elbows, not wrists. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Shrug
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for traps, grip using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides. 2) Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears. 3) Lower them slowly to a relaxed but controlled position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move vertically rather than rolling the shoulders, and keep your neck long. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps, forearms using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing forward. 2) Bend your elbows to curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders. 3) Lower the dumbbells fully with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep elbows close to your ribs and avoid swinging your torso. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Alternating Dumbbell Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps, forearms using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Stand holding dumbbells at your sides. 2) Curl one dumbbell toward your shoulder while the other arm stays long. 3) Lower it fully, then curl the other side. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep wrists neutral and make each side work through the same range. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps using dumbbell and chair.
Steps: 1) Sit on a chair, lean forward slightly, and brace one elbow against the inside of the thigh. 2) Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without moving the upper arm. 3) Lower the dumbbell slowly and repeat before switching sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the movement strict and avoid bouncing off the thigh. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Zottman Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps, forearms using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Curl dumbbells upward with palms facing up. 2) At the top, rotate palms to face down. 3) Lower slowly with palms down, then rotate back to palms up at the bottom. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use lighter weights than normal curls and control the rotation. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for forearms, biceps using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing your thighs. 2) Curl the dumbbells upward while keeping palms facing down. 3) Lower slowly to the start position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep wrists straight and use a lighter load than regular curls. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, upper back, biceps using pull-up bar and resistance band.
Steps: 1) Loop a resistance band securely around a pull-up bar and place one foot or knee in the band. 2) Start from a controlled hang and pull your chest toward the bar. 3) Lower yourself until arms are straight again. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Check the band and anchor first, and keep your ribs down instead of kicking for momentum. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Chair-Assisted Pull-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, upper back, biceps using pull-up bar and chair.
Steps: 1) Place a sturdy chair under a pull-up bar and keep one or both feet lightly on it. 2) Pull your body upward while using only as much leg help as needed. 3) Lower slowly to the starting position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Let the upper body do the work and keep the chair from sliding. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Negative Pull-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, upper back, biceps using pull-up bar or sturdy bar.
Steps: 1) Use a chair or jump carefully to start with your chin over the bar. 2) Hold briefly, then lower yourself as slowly as possible to straight arms. 3) Step back to the top position and repeat for low reps. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Do not drop quickly at the bottom; stop before grip or shoulder control fails. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Chin-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, biceps, upper back using pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Hang from a pull-up bar with palms facing you and hands about shoulder-width apart. 2) Pull your elbows down and bring your chest toward the bar. 3) Lower with control until arms are straight. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start each rep from a stable shoulder position and avoid kicking your legs. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, biceps, upper back using neutral-grip pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Hang from parallel handles with palms facing each other. 2) Pull your body upward by driving elbows down toward your ribs. 3) Lower slowly to a controlled hang. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your neck relaxed and use assistance if you cannot control the lower. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Scapular Pull-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lower traps, lats, shoulder control using pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Hang from a bar with arms straight and shoulders relaxed but controlled. 2) Without bending elbows, pull your shoulder blades down to lift your body slightly. 3) Relax back to the starting hang with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep reps small and precise; the elbows should stay straight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Flexed-Arm Hang
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for lats, biceps, grip using pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Use a chair to get your chin over a pull-up bar. 2) Hold the top position with elbows bent and chest close to the bar. 3) Step down safely when the hold is over or before form fails. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders packed down and avoid craning your chin over the bar. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Active Hang
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for grip, lats, shoulder stabilizers using pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart. 2) Gently pull shoulders down away from ears without bending your elbows much. 3) Hold for the target time, then step down safely. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a chair for partial support if your grip or shoulders are not ready for full bodyweight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dead Hang Grip Hold
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for grip, forearms, shoulders using pull-up bar.
Steps: 1) Grip a pull-up bar and hang with arms straight. 2) Keep your body quiet and hold for a comfortable time. 3) Step down before grip fully fails. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Do not relax into painful shoulder positions; use feet on a chair if needed. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Towel Grip Hang
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for grip, forearms, lats using pull-up bar and towel.
Steps: 1) Loop a sturdy towel over a pull-up bar and grip both ends. 2) Hang with controlled shoulders and a still body. 3) Hold for the target time, then step down carefully. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a strong towel and secure bar; this is much harder on grip than a normal hang. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Bent-Knee Inverted Row Under Table
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for upper back, lats, biceps using sturdy table.
Steps: 1) Lie under a sturdy table, grip the edge, and bend your knees with feet flat. 2) Pull your chest toward the table edge while keeping hips lifted or body straight. 3) Lower until arms are straight again. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Only use a table that cannot tip and keep your body rigid during the pull. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for back, lats, biceps using sturdy table and chair.
Steps: 1) Set your feet on a chair and grip a sturdy table edge or low bar. 2) Keep your body straight and pull your chest toward your hands. 3) Lower under control to straight arms. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Verify both supports are stable and keep glutes engaged so hips do not sag. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for back, lats, biceps using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Hold the handles and lean back with arms straight and body in a straight line. 2) Pull your chest toward the handles by driving elbows back. 3) Lower yourself until arms are straight again. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Walk feet forward to make it harder and keep shoulders away from ears. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer High Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for upper back, rear shoulders using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Lean back holding the suspension handles with arms straight at shoulder height. 2) Pull handles toward your upper chest with elbows high and wide. 3) Extend arms to lower back to the start. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep wrists straight and avoid shrugging as elbows move out. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer Face Pull
Target Area: Rear shoulders, rotator cuff, upper back
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, rotator cuff, upper back using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Hold the handles and lean back with arms extended in front of your face. 2) Pull the handles toward your temples while elbows bend and flare out. 3) Return slowly to arms straight. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your ribs down and finish with hands near your face, not low by your chest. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer Y Raise
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lower traps, shoulders using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Hold the handles and lean back with arms straight in front of you. 2) Raise your arms overhead into a Y shape to pull your body slightly forward. 3) Lower back to the start with straight arms. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Stand more upright to reduce difficulty and avoid arching your back. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer Rear-Delt Fly
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, upper back using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Lean back holding the handles with palms facing each other. 2) Open your arms out wide until your body moves forward between the handles. 3) Bring arms back together slowly. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep elbows slightly bent and use a body angle that lets you control the return. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suspension Trainer Biceps Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps, forearms, core using suspension trainer.
Steps: 1) Face the anchor, lean back, and hold handles with palms up and arms straight. 2) Curl your hands toward your forehead while keeping elbows high. 3) Extend your arms to lower your body back. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your body in one line and do not let elbows drop as you curl. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band Hammer Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for biceps, brachialis, forearms using resistance band.
Steps: 1) Stand on the middle of a band and hold the ends with palms facing each other. 2) Curl your hands toward your shoulders while keeping elbows near your sides. 3) Lower slowly until arms are straight. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep wrists neutral and avoid leaning back as tension increases. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band Reverse Curl
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for forearms, biceps using resistance band.
Steps: 1) Stand on a band and hold the ends with palms facing down. 2) Curl your hands upward while maintaining the palms-down grip. 3) Lower with control to the start position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a light band and keep wrists straight throughout. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band Upright Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for shoulders, upper traps using resistance band.
Steps: 1) Stand on a band and hold the ends in front of your thighs. 2) Pull elbows upward and outward until hands reach lower chest height. 3) Lower slowly to the start. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Stop below shoulder height if you feel shoulder pinching and keep wrists lower than elbows. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band Seated Face Pull
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, upper back using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Sit facing a band anchored at about face height and hold both ends. 2) Pull the band toward your face with elbows high. 3) Return arms forward slowly. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep chest tall and squeeze shoulder blades without jutting your head forward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Band Kneeling Row
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for back, lats, biceps using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band in front of you and kneel tall holding the ends. 2) Pull elbows back toward your ribs while staying tall through your hips. 3) Extend arms forward again under control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Squeeze glutes lightly so you do not lean back to finish the row. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tall-Kneeling Band Pullover
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, core using resistance band and high anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band high in front of you and kneel tall holding the ends with arms overhead. 2) Pull the band down in an arc toward your thighs while keeping arms mostly straight. 3) Return arms overhead slowly. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep ribs down and avoid turning it into a triceps pressdown. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Door-Anchor Lat Pulldown
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for lats, upper back, biceps using resistance band and door anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band high in a closed door and kneel or sit facing the anchor. 2) Pull elbows down toward your ribs as the band comes toward your chest. 3) Let arms reach back overhead with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Make sure the door anchor is secure and keep shoulders down as you pull. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Door-Anchor Face Pull
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for rear shoulders, upper back using resistance band and door anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band at about face height and hold the ends with arms straight. 2) Pull the band toward your face while elbows travel wide. 3) Return slowly to the start position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep wrists aligned with forearms and avoid leaning back to create movement. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Towel Prone Row with Lift-Off
Short Description: An at-home strength exercise for upper back, lats, shoulders using towel.
Steps: 1) Lie face down holding a towel with hands wider than shoulders and arms overhead. 2) Lift your chest slightly and pull the towel toward your collarbone. 3) Reach the towel forward again and lower gently if needed. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your neck long and make the lift small enough to avoid low-back strain. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Dead Bug Press
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for deep core, shoulders using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back in tabletop with knees over hips and hold one dumbbell above your chest. 2) Press the dumbbell straight up while slowly extending one leg toward the floor. 3) Bring the leg back to tabletop and repeat on the other side. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your low back gently heavy on the floor and do not let the dumbbell drift behind you. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Pullover Dead Bug
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for deep core, lats, hip flexors using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back in tabletop holding a light dumbbell over your chest with both hands. 2) Lower the dumbbell behind your head as one heel reaches toward the floor. 3) Return the dumbbell and leg to the start, then alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a light weight and shorten the range if your ribs flare or back arches. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Hollow Hold
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, hip flexors using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back holding a light dumbbell over your chest or slightly overhead. 2) Lift shoulders and legs into a hollow body shape. 3) Hold for the target time, then lower with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Choose a leg height that keeps your low back from lifting off the floor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs, hip flexors using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Sit with knees bent and hold one dumbbell close to your chest. 2) Lean back slightly and rotate your torso to one side. 3) Rotate through center to the other side, keeping the weight controlled. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Turn your chest, not just your arms, and keep the weight close if your back feels strained. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Sit-Up
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, hip flexors using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back with knees bent and hold a dumbbell at your chest. 2) Curl your torso up to a seated position. 3) Lower back to the floor one segment at a time. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the dumbbell close and avoid yanking your neck forward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Toe Reach
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for upper abs, hip flexors using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back with legs raised and a light dumbbell held over your chest. 2) Reach the dumbbell toward your toes by lifting your shoulder blades. 3) Lower your shoulders back down with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the motion small and lead with your ribs rather than swinging the arms. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Side Bend
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, quadratus lumborum using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Stand tall holding one dumbbell at your side and the other hand on your hip. 2) Slowly bend sideways toward the dumbbell. 3) Use the opposite side of your waist to return to tall standing. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move in a narrow side-bending path and avoid twisting or leaning forward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Around-the-Body Pass
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders, grip using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold a kettlebell in one hand. 2) Pass the kettlebell around your waist from hand to hand. 3) Continue circling, then reverse directions after the target reps. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your torso still and pass close to the body without clipping your hips. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Half-Kneeling Kettlebell Halo
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders, upper back using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Set up half-kneeling and hold a kettlebell by the horns near your chest. 2) Circle the kettlebell slowly around your head like a halo. 3) Bring it back to the front and continue, then switch directions and leg positions. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your ribs down and move around the head without pushing your head forward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Windmill
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, shoulders, hips using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Press or hold a kettlebell overhead with one arm and turn both feet slightly away from that arm. 2) Push your hips toward the loaded side and slide your free hand down the inside of the front leg. 3) Return to standing while keeping your eyes near the kettlebell. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start unloaded or very light and keep the overhead shoulder packed and steady. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Turkish Get-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength skill exercise for full body, core, shoulders, hips using kettlebell or dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back holding a light weight straight above one shoulder with the same-side knee bent. 2) Roll to your elbow, post to your hand, bridge your hips, and sweep the opposite leg under you. 3) Come to half-kneeling, stand up, then reverse each step back to the floor. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Practice unloaded first and keep eyes on the weight until you have strong shoulder control. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Half Turkish Get-Up
Short Description: An at-home strength skill exercise for core, shoulders, hips using kettlebell or dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Start on your back with one arm vertical and same-side knee bent. 2) Roll to elbow, then hand, bridge, and sweep the leg to half-kneeling. 3) Reverse the path back to your back before switching sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move one step at a time and pause whenever your shoulder or trunk position feels unstable. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tall Sit-Up to Press
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, shoulders, triceps using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back with knees bent and hold one dumbbell at your chest. 2) Sit up tall, then press the dumbbell overhead. 3) Lower the dumbbell to your chest and roll back down. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Finish the sit-up before pressing so you do not arch your back to move the weight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Bear Crawl Backpack Drag
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders, lats using backpack.
Steps: 1) Set up in a bear plank with a backpack on the floor outside one hand. 2) Reach the opposite hand under your body and drag the backpack to the other side. 3) Place the hand down and repeat in the other direction. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees close to the floor and resist rocking your hips as the bag moves. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Plank Backpack Drag
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders, lats using backpack.
Steps: 1) Set up in a high plank with a backpack outside one hand. 2) Reach the opposite hand under your torso and drag the backpack across. 3) Return the hand to the floor and alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Widen your feet and keep hips square to the floor throughout. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: High Plank Dumbbell Drag
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders, lats using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Place a dumbbell outside one hand and set up in a high plank. 2) Drag the dumbbell under your body to the opposite side with the far hand. 3) Reset the hand and repeat back across. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a dumbbell that slides safely or lift it carefully so it does not catch on the floor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Plank Pull-Through with Towel
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, shoulders using towel.
Steps: 1) Put a small towel on the floor beside one hand and start in a high plank. 2) Reach across with the opposite hand and pull the towel to the other side. 3) Place your hand down and repeat in the other direction. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move slowly and keep feet wide enough to stop your hips from twisting. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Plank
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, shoulders, glutes using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Place forearms on a stability ball and step feet back into a plank. 2) Brace your body in a straight line from head to heels. 3) Hold for the target time, then step forward carefully. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the ball under your elbows and avoid letting your hips sag. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Stir-the-Pot
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, shoulders, obliques using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Set forearms on a stability ball and step into a plank. 2) Make small circles with your forearms while your body stays still. 3) Circle both directions for the planned reps or time. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start with tiny circles and keep glutes squeezed to protect your low back. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Rollout
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, lats, shoulders using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Kneel on a mat with forearms on a stability ball. 2) Roll the ball forward by extending your hips and shoulders as one unit. 3) Pull the ball back under your shoulders using your abs and lats. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep ribs tucked and only roll as far as you can return without back arching. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Jackknife
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, hip flexors, shoulders using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Place your shins on a stability ball and hands on the floor in a high plank. 2) Pull knees toward your chest, rolling the ball forward. 3) Extend legs back to the plank position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders stacked over hands and avoid letting the ball shoot away. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Pike
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, shoulders, hip flexors using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Start in a high plank with feet or shins on a stability ball. 2) Lift your hips toward the ceiling and roll the ball toward your hands. 3) Lower back to a straight plank with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep legs as straight as you can control and avoid collapsing through the shoulders. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Stability Ball Dead Bug Squeeze
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for deep core, hip flexors using stability ball.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back and hold a stability ball between your hands and knees. 2) Press hands and knees lightly into the ball. 3) Extend one arm and the opposite leg away, then return and alternate. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the ball steady and your low back gently pressed toward the floor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kneeling Ab Wheel Rollout
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, lats, shoulders using ab wheel.
Steps: 1) Kneel on a mat holding an ab wheel under your shoulders. 2) Roll forward slowly while keeping hips and ribs connected. 3) Pull the wheel back under you using your abs and lats. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start with a very short range and stop before your low back arches. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kneeling Towel Body Saw
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, shoulders using towel or sliders.
Steps: 1) Set up in a forearm plank from your knees with a towel under your forearms or knees. 2) Slide your body slightly forward and backward like a small saw. 3) Return to center and continue for controlled reps. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the range small and maintain a straight line from knees to shoulders. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kneeling Band Crunch
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs using resistance band and high anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band overhead and kneel facing away or toward the anchor while holding the ends near your shoulders. 2) Curl your ribs toward your pelvis against the band tension. 3) Return to tall kneeling slowly. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep hips still and make the movement come from your trunk, not your arms pulling down. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Standing Band Crunch
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs using resistance band and high anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band overhead and hold it near your shoulders while standing. 2) Brace and crunch your ribs downward toward your pelvis. 3) Slowly return to tall standing. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees soft and avoid bending mostly at the hips. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tall-Kneeling Band Chop
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs, shoulders using resistance band and high anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band high to one side and kneel tall holding the band with both hands. 2) Pull the band diagonally down across your body toward the opposite hip. 3) Return to the high starting position with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep hips facing forward and rotate through your upper trunk. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tall-Kneeling Band Lift
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, shoulders, core using resistance band and low anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band low to one side and kneel tall holding it with both hands. 2) Lift the band diagonally upward across your body. 3) Return to the low start position slowly. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep glutes squeezed and do not let the band twist your hips. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Half-Kneeling Band Lift
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, shoulders, hip stability using resistance band and low anchor.
Steps: 1) Set up half-kneeling with a band anchored low to the side of your back knee. 2) Hold the band with both hands and lift diagonally across your body. 3) Return slowly to the anchor side. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the front knee steady and ribs stacked over the pelvis. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Standing Band Wood Chop High-to-Low
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs, hips using resistance band and high anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band high to one side and stand sideways to it with both hands on the band. 2) Pull diagonally down across your body as your torso rotates. 3) Return slowly to the high start position and repeat before switching sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Pivot your feet if needed and keep the motion controlled rather than jerky. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Standing Band Wood Chop Low-to-High
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs, shoulders using resistance band and low anchor.
Steps: 1) Anchor a band low to one side and stand sideways holding it with both hands. 2) Drive the band diagonally upward across your body. 3) Return slowly to the low start position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders down and rotate through the trunk without over-twisting your knees. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pallof Press March
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, deep core, hips using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways to a chest-height band anchor and press the band straight out in front of your chest. 2) Hold the press while lifting one knee at a time in a slow march. 3) Bring each foot back down quietly and keep the band centered. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a stance and band tension that let your torso stay square without leaning. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pallof Press Overhead Reach
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs, shoulders using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways to a band anchor and press the band straight out from your chest. 2) Keeping arms straight, raise your hands overhead slightly. 3) Bring hands back to chest height and then return the band to your chest. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep ribs down and do not let the band rotate your body. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: High Plank Knee Tap to Opposite Elbow
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, obliques, shoulders using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders. 2) Draw one knee toward the opposite elbow and pause briefly. 3) Return the foot to plank and alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders over hands and move the knee slowly instead of hopping. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Side Plank Band Row
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, lats, shoulders using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Set up in a side plank facing a band anchor with the top hand holding the band. 2) Hold hips up and row the band toward your ribs. 3) Extend the arm forward again while maintaining the side plank. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use light tension and keep hips stacked rather than rolling toward the floor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Side Plank Band Rotation
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, shoulders using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Set up in a side plank with a band held in the top hand. 2) Rotate your top arm slightly open against the band while keeping hips lifted. 3) Return to the starting position with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the rotation small and avoid pulling with the neck or lower back. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Full Copenhagen Side Plank
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for adductors, obliques, shoulders using chair or couch.
Steps: 1) Place the top foot or ankle on a sturdy chair and set up on your side elbow. 2) Lift hips and bring the bottom leg up toward the supported leg if able. 3) Hold for the target time, then lower carefully. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start with the knee supported and stop if the inner thigh feels strained. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Hollow Body Band Pulldown
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for abs, lats, shoulders using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back holding a band anchored behind your head and set your legs in a hollow position. 2) Pull the band down toward your thighs while keeping shoulders and legs lifted. 3) Return arms overhead with control without losing the hollow shape. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Choose a hollow position that keeps your low back down and ribs tucked. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pilates Criss-Cross
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for obliques, abs using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back with hands behind your head and knees in tabletop. 2) Rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends. 3) Switch sides in a controlled bicycle-like rhythm. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep elbows wide and rotate from the ribs instead of pulling on your neck. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pilates Corkscrew
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for lower abs, obliques using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Lie on your back with legs extended toward the ceiling and arms pressing into the floor. 2) Circle both legs to one side, down slightly, across, and back to center. 3) Repeat in the other direction while keeping your upper body steady. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Make the circle small enough that your low back stays controlled. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pilates Leg Pull Front
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, glutes, shoulders using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Start in a high plank with feet hip-width apart. 2) Lift one straight leg a few inches without shifting your hips. 3) Lower it and alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Push the floor away and keep the lift small and glute-driven. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Pilates Leg Pull Back
Short Description: An at-home core strength exercise for core, glutes, shoulders using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Sit with hands behind you, fingers facing your feet or slightly outward, and lift into a reverse plank. 2) Lift one leg a few inches while keeping hips high. 3) Lower the leg and alternate sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep chest open and avoid sinking into your shoulders. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: RKC Plank
Short Description: An at-home isometric strength exercise for abs, glutes, shoulders using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders and feet slightly apart. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull elbows lightly toward toes, and brace as if preparing for a cough. 3) Hold this high-tension plank for a short time, then rest. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) This should feel intense quickly; keep the hold short and do not let your back sag. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Thruster
Short Description: An at-home conditioning strength exercise for full body, quads, shoulders using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hold dumbbells at your shoulders with feet shoulder-width apart. 2) Squat down, then stand powerfully and press the dumbbells overhead. 3) Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders and flow into the next rep. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the squat and press connected, but maintain control instead of racing sloppy reps. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Hang Clean
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, hips, upper back using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs and hinge slightly at the hips. 2) Drive your hips forward and guide the dumbbells up to your shoulders. 3) Stand tall in the catch, then lower back to the hang position. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use hip drive more than arm curling and keep the dumbbells close to your body. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Clean to Press
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, shoulders, hips using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Start with dumbbells at your sides or in front of your thighs. 2) Clean them to your shoulders using a small hip drive. 3) Press overhead, lower to shoulders, then lower back to the start. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Separate clean and press if needed and avoid arching your back overhead. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Snatch
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, hips, shoulders using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Place one dumbbell between your feet and hinge down to grip it with one hand. 2) Drive through your legs and pull the dumbbell close to your body. 3) Punch it overhead in one motion, then lower safely and switch sides as planned. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a light weight while learning and keep the dumbbell path close, not looping away. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Alternating Dumbbell Snatch
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, hips, shoulders using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Set one dumbbell on the floor between your feet. 2) Snatch it overhead with one hand, then lower it back to the floor. 3) Switch hands on the floor and repeat on the other side. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Reset your hinge each rep and keep the floor area clear. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Suitcase March
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for core, grip, hips using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Hold one dumbbell at your side and stand tall. 2) March in place by lifting one knee at a time. 3) Continue for time, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Stay tall and resist leaning toward the weight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Dumbbell Farmer March
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for grip, traps, core, hips using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall. 2) March in place with slow, deliberate knee lifts. 3) Keep marching for the target time, then set the weights down safely. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders down and steps quiet rather than stomping. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Swing
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for glutes, hamstrings, core using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Stand with feet slightly wider than hips and the kettlebell in front of you. 2) Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap your hips forward. 3) Let the kettlebell float to chest height and guide it back into the next hinge. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a hip hinge, keep arms relaxed, and stop before fatigue makes your back round. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Clean
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for hips, glutes, upper back using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Start with a kettlebell between your feet or from a short backswing. 2) Drive through your hips and guide the bell up close to your body. 3) Catch it softly in the rack position at your forearm and shoulder. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the bell close so it does not slam your wrist; practice with light weight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, shoulders, hips using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Clean a kettlebell to the rack position at your shoulder. 2) Brace your core and press it overhead. 3) Lower to the rack, then back to the start before repeating or switching sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Own the rack position before pressing and keep your wrist straight. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell High Pull
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for hips, upper back, shoulders using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Start like a one-arm kettlebell swing with the bell between your legs. 2) Drive the hips forward and pull the elbow back high as the bell rises. 3) Guide the bell back into the next backswing. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the pull close to the body and avoid yanking with the shoulder. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Figure-Eight Pass
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for core, hips, coordination using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Stand with feet wider than hips and hold a kettlebell in one hand. 2) Hinge slightly and pass the kettlebell between your legs to the other hand. 3) Continue weaving it in a figure-eight pattern around both legs. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your back flat and start slow so you do not clip your knees. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Medicine Ball Slam
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for full body, abs, shoulders using medicine ball.
Steps: 1) Stand with a medicine ball held overhead or at chest height. 2) Rise tall, then slam the ball down in front of you using your whole body. 3) Pick it up safely and repeat. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a slam-safe ball and surface, and keep your spine neutral as you retrieve it. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Medicine Ball Rotational Slam
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for obliques, hips, shoulders using medicine ball.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways to a safe slam area holding a medicine ball. 2) Rotate through your hips and trunk to slam the ball down outside one foot. 3) Pick it up, reset, and repeat before switching sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Pivot your feet and avoid twisting only through your knees or low back. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Mini-Band Fast Feet
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for glutes, calves, cardio using mini band.
Steps: 1) Place a mini band above your knees and sink into a small athletic stance. 2) Move your feet quickly in place while keeping knees pressing gently outward. 3) Continue for the interval, staying low and controlled. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep steps small and do not let the band pull your knees inward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Agility Ladder In-In-Out-Out
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for feet, calves, coordination using agility ladder or tape lines.
Steps: 1) Stand at one end of an agility ladder or taped squares. 2) Step both feet into a square, then both feet outside the square. 3) Move forward through the ladder with a steady rhythm. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Stay light on the balls of your feet and prioritize clean foot placement over speed. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Agility Ladder Ickey Shuffle
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for feet, hips, coordination using agility ladder or tape lines.
Steps: 1) Stand beside the first ladder square. 2) Step inside with one foot, inside with the other, then outside to the far side. 3) Repeat the three-step pattern down the ladder. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Start slow until the pattern is automatic and keep your hips low. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Agility Ladder Lateral In-Out
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for calves, hips, coordination using agility ladder or tape lines.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways at the end of a ladder or line of squares. 2) Step both feet into the square, then both feet out on the far side. 3) Continue laterally through each square. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep your chest up and feet quick but quiet. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Agility Ladder Ali Shuffle
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for calves, coordination, cardio using agility ladder or tape line.
Steps: 1) Stand with one foot ahead of a line and one foot behind it. 2) Quickly switch foot positions like a boxer shuffle. 3) Continue down the ladder or stay over one line for time. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees soft and land lightly on the balls of your feet. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Step-Up Burpee
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for full body, legs, shoulders using low step.
Steps: 1) Stand facing a low step with room behind you. 2) Place hands on the step, step or jump feet back to plank, then return feet forward. 3) Stand up and step onto the platform or reach overhead. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use the step to reduce impact and keep hands firmly planted before moving your feet. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Plank Jack to Squat Stand
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for full body, core, legs using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Start in a high plank with feet together. 2) Jump or step feet out and in once like a plank jack. 3) Step or jump feet toward hands and stand, then return to plank. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the plank tight before transitioning and use step-outs for a lower-impact version. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Invisible Rope Double-Under Hop
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for calves, cardio, coordination using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Stand tall with elbows near your sides as if holding a jump rope. 2) Perform a slightly higher hop while rotating your wrists twice quickly. 3) Land softly and reset for the next hop or continuous rhythm. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep jumps springy and low enough to protect your calves and Achilles. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Shadow Boxing Sprawl
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for full body, chest, core using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Start in a boxing stance and throw a short punch combo. 2) Place hands on the floor and shoot both legs back into a sprawl or plank. 3) Step or hop feet forward and return to your boxing stance. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the floor transition controlled and step back instead of jumping if needed. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Low-Impact Dumbbell Step Jack
Short Description: An at-home conditioning exercise for shoulders, hips, cardio using light dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hold very light dumbbells at your sides or shoulders and stand tall. 2) Step one foot out as you raise the dumbbells outward or overhead. 3) Step back in and alternate sides in a steady rhythm. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use very light weights and keep the arm range pain-free. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Kettlebell Deadlift High Pull
Short Description: An at-home power conditioning exercise for hips, upper back, shoulders using kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Start with the kettlebell between your feet and hinge to grip the handle. 2) Stand powerfully and pull the kettlebell up toward chest height with elbows high. 3) Lower it back between your feet with a controlled hinge. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the bell close and avoid pulling higher than your shoulders tolerate. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg RDL with Dumbbell Pass
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for hamstrings, glutes, balance using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Balance on one leg and hinge forward with a dumbbell in one hand. 2) At the bottom of the hinge, pass the dumbbell to the other hand under your chest. 3) Stand back up, then repeat or alternate passes. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep hips square and make the pass slow enough that balance stays controlled. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg Balance with Overhead Press
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for ankles, hips, shoulders, core using dumbbell or bottle.
Steps: 1) Stand on one leg holding a light weight at shoulder height. 2) Press the weight overhead while keeping the standing knee softly bent. 3) Lower the weight and continue pressing or switch sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use a light load and touch a wall if your balance causes torso leaning. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg Halo
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for ankles, hips, core, shoulders using kettlebell or dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Balance on one leg holding a light weight at chest height. 2) Circle the weight slowly around your head. 3) Return it to the front and repeat before switching directions or legs. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Make the circle small and keep the standing foot rooted. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg Pallof Press
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for obliques, hips, ankle stability using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways to a band anchor and balance on the leg farther from the anchor. 2) Hold the band at your chest, then press it straight out. 3) Bring it back to your chest without letting your body rotate. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use light band tension and prioritize balance over distance from the anchor. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tandem Pallof Press
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for core, hips, foot stability using resistance band and anchor.
Steps: 1) Stand heel-to-toe sideways to a band anchor and hold the band at your chest. 2) Press the band straight out in front of you. 3) Return to your chest and repeat before switching stance direction. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep both feet grounded and reduce band tension if your stance wobbles too much. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Lateral Step-Down with Forward Reach
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for quads, glutes, knee control using low step.
Steps: 1) Stand sideways on a low step with one foot hanging off the edge. 2) Reach both arms forward as you bend the standing knee and tap the free heel down. 3) Stand back up and reset your balance. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the reach from pulling your knee inward and use a low height first. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg Squat to Lateral Reach
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for quads, glutes, outer hips using no equipment.
Steps: 1) Balance on one leg with arms in front of you. 2) Bend the standing knee into a small squat while reaching the free leg out to the side. 3) Return to tall single-leg balance. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the squat shallow and the pelvis level as the free leg reaches. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Banded Star Balance
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for outer hips, ankles, core using mini band.
Steps: 1) Place a mini band above your knees or ankles and balance on one leg. 2) Reach the free foot forward, to the side, and backward like points of a star. 3) Return to center between each reach. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep tension in the band and avoid letting the standing knee collapse inward. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Cushion Single-Leg Stand
Short Description: An at-home balance exercise for ankles, feet, hips using cushion or pillow.
Steps: 1) Place one foot on a firm cushion and lift the other foot slightly. 2) Stand tall and hold your balance for the target time. 3) Step down safely and switch sides. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Stand near a wall and keep your gaze fixed on one point. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Cushion Tandem Stance
Short Description: An at-home balance exercise for feet, ankles, hips using cushion or pillow.
Steps: 1) Stand heel-to-toe on or near a firm cushion with a wall beside you. 2) Hold the tandem position while breathing steadily. 3) Switch which foot is in front after the hold. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Use light fingertip support and avoid locking your knees. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Single-Leg Calf Raise Eyes Closed
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for calves, ankles, balance using wall support optional.
Steps: 1) Stand on one leg near a wall and rise onto the ball of your foot. 2) Close your eyes only if you can do so safely and hold or perform a slow calf raise. 3) Open your eyes and lower the heel with control. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep one finger near the wall and stop if you feel unsafe or unstable. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Tandem Farmer March
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for grip, core, hips, feet using dumbbells.
Steps: 1) Hold dumbbells at your sides and stand as if on a narrow line. 2) March slowly by placing one foot directly in front of the other. 3) Continue for a few steps or in place, then turn carefully. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep shoulders level and use lighter weights than a normal farmer carry. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Waiter Carry March
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for shoulders, core, hips using dumbbell or kettlebell.
Steps: 1) Hold one light weight overhead with a straight arm and ribs down. 2) March in place slowly, lifting one knee at a time. 3) Switch arms after the target time. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the weight stacked over your shoulder and avoid leaning away from it. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Suitcase Carry March with Head Turns
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for core, grip, vestibular balance using dumbbell or backpack.
Steps: 1) Hold a weight in one hand and stand tall. 2) March in place while slowly turning your head left and right. 3) Switch the weight to the other hand and repeat. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move the head slowly and stop if dizziness occurs. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Half-Kneeling Press to Stand
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for glutes, quads, shoulders, core using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Start half-kneeling with a light dumbbell at shoulder height. 2) Press the dumbbell overhead, bring it back down, then stand up from the half-kneeling position. 3) Step back to half-kneeling with control and repeat. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Keep the front knee stable and avoid rushing the transition to standing. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Lunge Matrix with Dumbbell Pass
Short Description: An at-home balance strength exercise for legs, hips, core, coordination using dumbbell.
Steps: 1) Hold a light dumbbell at chest height and stand tall. 2) Step into a forward, side, or reverse lunge and pass the dumbbell around the front thigh or across your body. 3) Return to standing before changing lunge direction. 4) Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
Best Practices: 1) Move one direction at a time and keep the pass controlled so posture stays tall. 2) Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

Name: Beast Reach
Short Description: An at-home bodyweight control exercise for shoulders, core, hips using no equipment.
